vilayet_stats.vilayet: Yanya, Epirus and Albania part (Yanya, Ergiri, Berat and Preveze sancakları incl. Narda; Grebene kazası excluded). Sum of clusters
vilayet_stats.source: Kaza totals and Muslims for the territory Ottoman after 1881 come from the 1881/82-93 Ottoman census (Karpat 1978, IJMES 9: kaza table by sex and millet, 516,477 incl. 3,677 Jews). Narda's ceded part is from the 1878 Ottoman statistic (16,527 males x2 minus Loros, Kokolakis 2003 App. G/I). Muslim counts are raised to the 1870 Muslim:Christian ratios built from the 1871 Yanya salname (Kokolakis 2003 Table G21) for Chameria, the Leskovik group and Berat sancağı. Adds the 7,900 regular troops of the 1871 salname. Jews excluded. turk share in %.

vilayet_stats.vilayet: Yanya, Tırhala sancağı (Thessaly incl. Alasonya). Sum of clusters
vilayet_stats.source: Total: the 1878 count (Popović) in Serbestoğlu, Belleten (TTK), Table 1: 324,093 Christians+Muslims, Jews 4,090 excluded. Muslim shares by kaza, upper end: 1871 Yanya salname via Öncel (Yenişehir 29.67%, Çatalca 34.24%); Akyay 2001 table, read as male counts (Tırhala 4.2%, Kardiçe 6.7%); 1878 count (Golos 3.6%, Ermiye 19.3%, Velestin-Tırnova 38%); 1881/82-93 census (Alasonya 8.1%). Turk share follows Serbestoğlu (mostly Konya Turks, plus Albanians, Tatars and Circassians). turk share in %.

vilayet_stats.vilayet: Yanya, whole vilayet within this region (both rows above)
vilayet_stats.source: Sum of the two Yanya rows. For comparison, the 1880 state salname (vol. 36) registered 389,251 males (x2 = 778,502). Kokolakis 2003 p. 270.

Yanya salname 1288/1871 as given by A. Dumont, Le Balkan et l'Adriatique (1874) p. 335 (718,000 inhabitants, 251,000 Muslims, 'chiffre qui peut être considéré comme certain'). Ubicini & Pavet de Courteille, État présent de l'Empire ottoman (1876) p. 20 doubles these to 501,498 Muslims and 935,202 non-Muslims (1,436,700). Kokolakis shows that figure is an erroneous doubling. Includes Thessaly, whose 1871 figures were abnormally low.

vilayet_stats.vilayet: Yanya, Epirus part (reference: 1878 Ottoman statistic, males x2)
vilayet_stats.source: Official 1878 statistic (Mile 1986 no. 248, in Kokolakis 2003 n. 31 and App. G/I): 266,824 males = 104,239 Muslims + 160,678 Christians + ~1,900 others. Includes Narda and Grebene.
Karpat 1978, IJMES 9, Yanya province kaza table: 286,304 Greek Orthodox, 225,415 Muslims, 3,677 Jews. Used as the kaza base above.

vilayet_stats.vilayet: İşkodra, part within the bbox (İşkodra sancağı without Bar/Antivari, Spuž and Žabljak, plus Draç sancağı). Sum of clusters
vilayet_stats.source: Draç sancağı (Draç, Tiran, Kavaya, Şıak) and Akçahisar come from the 1881/82-93 census (Karpat 1978): 87,372 people, 78,600 Muslims. The İşkodra sancağı was not censused; its total follows İ. Erken (OTAM 40, 2016; MA thesis OMÜ 2014): vilayet about 250,000 with about 90,000 Christians, about 64% Muslim. Podgorica and Ulcinj (lost 1878-80) are added. The Muslim share is set at the upper end, 64%. Cross-checks: 1911 Ottoman figures 349,455 (218,089 Muslims = 62.4%); BOA PRK.MK 12/92 (1903) 320,000 (170,000 Muslims); Gawrych: 200,000-300,000 in the 1880s. turk share in %.

vilayet_stats.vilayet: İşkodra, Draç sancağı + Akçahisar kazası (reference, census)
vilayet_stats.source: Karpat 1978, İşkodra province table. Only these units were censused.

vilayet_stats.vilayet: Manastır, Görice sancağı without Kesriye (Görice, İstarova, Kolonya kazaları). Sum of clusters
vilayet_stats.source: Karpat 1978, Manastır province table: Görice 65,368 (32,759 Muslims), İstarova 24,134 (21,106), Kolonya 15,325 (9,511). TDV İA 'Görice': 1882 count for the whole sancak incl. Kesriye 76,489 Muslims / 50,742 Christians. In 1874-77 these kazas belonged to the newly formed Manastır vilayeti.

vilayet_stats.vilayet: Manastır, Elbasan (Elbasan, Peklin, Grameç, Şpat, Çermenika, Dumre). Sum of clusters
vilayet_stats.source: No Ottoman figure: Elbasan and Dibra were excluded from the 1881/82-93 census (Karpat 1978 footnote). The total is A. Rostkovski's 1897 figure (51,786 Muslim Albanians, 3,319 Christian Albanians, 1,000 Aromanians). The town share follows Sami Frashëri's Kamus-ül-Alam (16,500 Muslims / 3,500 Christians).

vilayet_stats.vilayet: Prizren, Albanian parts (Prizren sancağı: Has, Luma, Yakova highlands; Dibra sancağı: Mat, Dibra-i Zir, Martaneş-Bulqiza). Sum of clusters
vilayet_stats.source: Low-confidence estimate. Prizren and Dibra sancakları were not censused in 1881/82-93. For context: Ottoman records for 1895 give Prizren sancağı 73,708 Muslims / 24,101 Christians (Y. Ahbab / B. Tamaç thesis, Uludağ 2015). Gawrych gives Dibra sancağı 200,000; Rostkovski 1897 gives 82,644. Ubicini 1876 lists Prizren and Dibra under Manastır vilayeti (1874-77).

vilayet_stats.vilayet: Yunanistan, north of 38.3N. Sum of clusters
vilayet_stats.source: Greek census of June 1879 by nomarchy (Statesman's Year-Book 1881): Akarnania-Aitolia 138,444; Fokida-Fthiotida 128,440; Euboea-Sporades 95,136 (Karystia and Skyros excluded, 73,000 kept); Corfu 106,109 (incl. Lefkada and Paxoi; about 5,000 Jews excluded, 101,000 kept); Cephalonia 80,543 (northern part and Ithaca, 28,500 kept); Attica-Boeotia 185,364 (Boeotia part 45,000). The in-bbox shares are estimates.

sources: K. H. Karpat, 'Ottoman Population Records and the Census of 1881/82-1893', IJMES 9 (1978) 237-274, kaza tables (first-choice Ottoman source). Yanya: Yanya 85,558 (Muslims 4,759), Aydonat 14,592 (3,993), Filat 24,210 (9,720), Mecova 5,099 (0), Leskovik 18,311 (~4,750), Koniçe 16,570 (~1,431), Pogon 21,072 (953), Premedi 28,876 (18,461), Ergiri 30,689 (11,791), Delvine 19,991 (5,885), Tepedelen 25,915 (19,667), Kurvelesh 15,704 (10,536), Berat 107,843 (~72,155), Avlonya 29,615 (~25,057), Skrapar 11,719, Tomoriçe 7,815, Preveze 11,687 (1,611), Loros 16,253 (1,188), Margariç 24,956 (14,364). Görice sancağı: Görice 65,368, İstarova 24,134, Kolonya 15,325, Kesriye 60,900. İşkodra: Draç 4,780, Tiran 32,471, Kavaya 19,632, Şıak 16,277, Akçahisar ~14,192. Serfiçe: Alasonya 26,855 (2,188 Muslims).

caveats: There is no religion-by-kaza Ottoman count for 1876 itself. The Yanya kaza base is the 1881/82-93 Ottoman census, the nearest complete count with both sexes and millet by kaza. The 1875 salname gives only males and has known copying errors (Filat, Delvine, Tepedelen, Koniçe and Skrapar carry totals copied from 1871, per Kokolakis). The 1878 statistic gives males only, and its totals run about 6% below the census for the Muslim-majority north. Using the census therefore favours Muslim counts.

Kaza boundaries in 1876 differ from the census units used to sum the populations. Leskovik kazası was formed later from parts of Koniçe and Premedi. Kurvelesh/Himara was part of Delvine. Loros and Çumerka belonged to the Narda and Yanya kazas before 1881. About 25 Premedi villages passed to Kolonya after 1876. Lusnya/Fier was part of Berat. Populations therefore sum to the census units, with Narda's ceded part as a separate unit, not to exact 1876 kazas.

Thessaly totals conflict. The Ottoman registers doubled give only 218,484 (1875 salname, 109,242 males) or about 246,000 (1880 state salname). The 1871 salname figures for Thessaly are abnormally low (Kokolakis). The 1878 count (324,093) was used. Kaza splits inside its grouped rows follow Akyay's table, read as male counts (Golos x2 matches 1878 almost exactly). Dömeke's 9,000 and the Agrafa remainder (17,109) are residuals of the 1878 Kardiçe-Çatalca-Dömeke row and are low confidence.

Upper-end choice: Muslim counts are the census values raised to the 1870 ratios derived from the 1871 salname where those were higher (Chameria +8.8%, Leskovik group +6%, Berat sancağı +3.9%). In Thessaly the 1871 salname percentages for Yenişehir and Çatalca were used instead of the lower 1878 and Akyay values. The resulting Muslim total in Thessaly (43,812) is above the 1878 count (39,392) and EI2 (40,000).

Garrison: the 1871 Yanya salname gives 7,900 regular troops for the Epirus corps. Their split between battalion seats (Yanya 3,500, Narda 1,200, Ergiri 1,000, Berat 1,000, Avlonya 600, Preveze 600) and the 50/50 turk/other split are my allocation. No troops were added in Thessaly or İşkodra because no Ottoman figure was found.

turk vs muslim_other in Epirus and Albania: the registers say only 'İslam'. About 16,300 turk are placed in the towns (Yanya 27%, Berat 19%, Narda 19%, Avlonya 15%, Ergiri 15%, Preveze 10.5%, smaller towns 3-10%), guided by the Ottoman 1908 figure of about 20,000 'Turks' for the post-1881 vilayet. The individual town values are estimates, and most Muslims of Yanya, Preveze and the Albanian towns were Albanian- or Greek-speaking.

İşkodra sancağı (except Akçahisar), Elbasan, Dibra and the Prizren highlands were not counted in the 1881/82-93 census. Their totals are estimates bounded by Erken, the 1911 Ottoman figures, Gawrych and, for Elbasan only, Rostkovski. The cluster splits inside them are judgement calls (low/medium confidence). The İşkodra sancağı figure needs a Muslim share of about 52% to reach the 64% vilayet share; Western ethnographic estimates would give about 43%.

Overlaps with neighbouring datasets. Our Görice, Görice ovası and Devol clusters duplicate the Macedonia dataset's 'Görice kasabası ve ovası', so keep only one set. 'Yakova dağları (Tropojë)' partly overlaps the Kosovo dataset's 'Yakova (Gjakova)' circle. Has (Krumë) adjoins the Kosovo 'Has ve Podrima' cluster. Gollobordë was dropped because the Macedonia dataset has 'Golo Brdo'. Podgorica, Ulcinj and Luma are covered here because the Kosovo dataset left them out.

Grebene (Grevena) kazası belonged to Yanya vilayeti in the 1870s (16,941 males in 1878). It and Kesriye are in the Macedonia dataset and excluded from the totals here. Alasonya is counted in Tırhala sancağı (Karpat's 1877-78 list), although it later belonged to Serfiçe sancağı.

Jews are excluded: Yanya about 3,334 (census), Preveze about 200, Thessaly 4,090 (1878), and Narda and Corfu (about 5,000). Orthodox Albanians and Aromanians count as Christian. Crypto-Christians (Shpat) count as Muslim.
Narda's ceded part: the Muslim numbers in Arta town (1,400 civilians) are an estimate with no Ottoman kaza figure. Arta and Thessaly south of Elassona passed to Greece in 1881.

Kingdom of Greece: the 1879 nomarchy totals are official, but the shares inside the bounding box (Boeotia, Euboea without Karystia and Skyros, northern Kefalonia plus Ithaca) and the eparchy splits are estimates. Muslims there are set to 0.

Circassian and Tatar settlers in Thessaly (1874-76, Sfika-Theodosiou, Egnatia 1, 1989) and Circassians elsewhere could not be quantified from an Ottoman or Turkish source, so nothing was added beyond the 1878 count. The Velestin and Ermiye clusters carry a muslim_other share for them.
Lakes Karla and Copais still existed in 1876. The Boeotia centre was moved south of Copais. The Karla-side circles (Yenişehir doğusu, Velestin) may touch the lake.
changes: Every cluster now has a population, a vilayet and a sancak. 142 clusters; total 1,912,034 (Ottoman part 1,397,650).

Yanya vilayeti kaza totals and Muslim counts were rebased on the 1881/82-93 Ottoman census (Karpat 1978), replacing the draft's qualitative shares. The draft's southern-Albanian Muslim shares were also checked against the 1871-salname ratios (Kokolakis Table G21), and the higher value was kept.

Chameria: Filat kazası 43.7% Muslim (census 40.1% raised to the 1871 ratio): Konispol 85%, Filat 55%, Gümenice 55% (draft 75%), eastern villages 3.4%. Aydonat 29.8% (town cluster 40%, draft 55%; Orta Çamlık 45%, draft 60%). Margariç kazası 62.6% (Margariti villages 90%, draft 75%; Fener 41%, draft 25%; Parga 8%).

Leskovik split in two after the census (kaza 27.5% Muslim): the town with its Muslim villages at 55% (draft 60%), and a new Christian 'Leskovik güneyi / Gramoz' cluster at 6%. Koniçe town 55.5% Muslim with 8.3% turk; the kaza is 9.2% Muslim (census).
Premedi kazası 67.8% Muslim (census 63.9% raised to the 1870 ratio): town 62%, Frashër-Këlcyrë 88% (draft 70%), southern Orthodox villages 25%.

Ergiri sancağı uses census shares. Ergiri kaza 38.4% plus garrison (town 73% Muslim, draft 72%; Riza-Kardhiq 91.5%). Delvine 29.4% (town 55%; Lukovë-Borsh 33%, draft 50%). Tepedelen 75.9% (draft 85%). Kurvelesh 95% and Himara 5.6%, giving the census kaza value of 67.1%.

Berat sancağı raised to the 1870 ratio of 333 Muslims per 100 Christians (76.6% overall): Berat kaza 69.5% (town 67.7% with 19% turk; rural 74%, draft 60%; Lusnya 75%, draft 65%; Mallakastra 95%; Myzeqe 51% and Fier 51%, draft 50%). Avlonya kazası 87.9% (town 88%, rural 94.5%, draft 85%). Skrapar 97.1% and Tomoriçe 96.6% (census).
'Grameş / Tomoriça' was split. Tomoriçe is now a separate Berat-sancağı cluster (7,815, census); Grameç stays in Elbasan.
Garrison added: the 7,900 regular troops of the 1871 Yanya salname, placed at the battalion seats, half turk and half muslim_other.

Turkish-speaking element raised in the Epirus and Albanian towns, following the Ottoman 1908 figure of about 20,000 Turks for Yanya vilayeti: Yanya town turk 27% (draft 8%), Berat 19% (2%), Narda 19% (10%), Avlonya 15% (3%), Ergiri 15% (2%), Preveze 10.5% (8%), Delvine and Premedi 10% (0%), Koniçe 8%.

Yanya kazası: town 44% Muslim (draft 38%), giving the census figure of 4,759 civil Muslims plus 3,500 troops. Added a 'Malakasi nahiyesi' cluster (Christian), because Kokolakis's nahiye shares show Malakasi as about 22% of the kaza's rural population.

Thessaly totals come from the 1878 count (Serbestoğlu/Belleten). Kaza Muslim shares are set at the upper end: Yenişehir 29.67% (1871 salname/Öncel): Larissa town 60% Muslim (54% turk), Konyar villages 46% (draft 42%), Velestin 45% (draft 40%), Tırnova 30% (draft 33%), Enipeas 20% (draft 33%), Pinios 8% (draft 14%). Çatalca 34.24% (town 50%, plain 29.6%; draft 44% and 31%). Golos 3.6% (Volos town 26.7%, draft 18%). Ermiye 19.3%. Tırhala 4.2% (town 25%, draft 31%). Kardiçe 6.7% (town 25%, draft 28%). Alasonya 8.1% (town 30%, draft 33%). Dömeke 10% (draft 22%; no Ottoman figure). About 89% of Thessaly's Muslims are counted as turk (Konyar; Serbestoğlu).

İşkodra vilayeti. The Draç sancağı kazas were set to census values: Kavaya 86% Muslim (draft 97%), Draç 63% (68%), Tiran town 92.8% and villages 99.6%, Şıak 90.7%, Krujë 99% (88%), Kurbin 67% (50%). The İşkodra sancağı was raised so the vilayet reaches 64% Muslim (Erken; 1911 Ottoman 62.4%): Shkodër town 81% (draft 73%; Lear and Sami hane counts give 82%), Postrip 85% (65%), Bregu i Bunës and Ana e Malit 78% (60%), Podgorica 80% (71%), Ulcinj 88% (82%), Tuzi 45% (35%), Kastrati 33% (30%), Puka 48% (25%), Zadrima 28% (15%), Lezhë 50% (35%), Lower Dukagjin 18% (15%).

Görice sancağı uses census values: Görice kaza 50.1% Muslim (Devoll 70%, draft 65%; town 30%, draft 35%; plain 45%; Opar 85%). İstarova 87.5% (Pogradec area 78%, draft 62%; Mokra 97%). Kolonya 62.1% (draft 75%).

Elbasan raised to 92.3% Muslim overall (town 82.5% after Kamus, draft 77%; Shpat and plain 94%, draft 93%). Has 88% (draft 85%) and Tropojë 90% (draft 88%); the other Prizren and Dibra highlands are unchanged.
Gollobordë was removed to avoid double-counting with the Macedonia dataset's 'Golo Brdo'.

Coordinates: Boeotia moved to 38.35N 23.05E, off the then-existing Lake Copais. Mesolongi moved to 38.42N 21.43E and northern Kefalonia to 38.33N 20.55E, both inland. New clusters were placed at Tomorricë (40.66N 20.22E), Malakasi (39.64N 21.06E) and the Pyrsogianni/Vourbiani area (40.21N 20.72E).
